issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. Only numpy and scipy are used, and the change only affects how the final radii are fixed.

The change is a real algorithmic step. A linear program (HiGHS) maximizes the sum of radii with the centres fixed, using 1e-12 margins on the pair-distance and wall limits. The existing shrink loop still runs afterwards and now has 300 iterations instead of 50. Any LP failure falls back to the old radii, so validity is still enforced. With 496 pair constraints for n=32 the LP is cheap, so the time limit is not at risk.

Recomputed z: (2.9370 - 2.9365) / (0.0034 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) ≈ 0.104. The harness gives 0.107, and the gap is explained by the inputs being rounded. The improvement of about 0.0005 is well inside the noise, and each side has only one run. The provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.
Minor: the result is near the best published value of about 2.9370, so further gains will be small. Confirming would take several replicates per side.
